_comment: Rows for the error-code lookup in the header (script.js, stOpenErrorCodes). Every row is copied from a Microsoft page that was fetched and read, named by its src key below; nothing is written from memory. 'code' is as Microsoft prints it: decimal for Windows Installer, hexadecimal for the rest. The lookup computes the negative decimal form and decodes 0x8007xxxx itself, so neither is stored. 'use' is the first thing to check, from the endpoint topic for the codes it explains and from Microsoft's own description for Intune's. Add a row only from a page you read; record the page under 'sources'.

cm.title: Application installation common error codes reference (Configuration Manager)

codes.name: ERROR_SUCCESS
codes.meaning: The action completed successfully.
codes.use: Success. Nothing to do.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_DATA
codes.meaning: The data is invalid.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER
codes.meaning: One of the parameters was invalid.

codes.name: ERROR_CALL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
codes.meaning: This value is returned when a custom action attempts to call a function that can't be called from custom actions. The function returns the value ERROR_CALL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

codes.name: ERROR_APPHELP_BLOCK
codes.meaning: If Windows Installer determines a product might be incompatible with the current operating system, it displays a dialog box informing the user and asking whether to try to install anyway. This error code is returned if the user chooses not to try the installation.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_SERVICE_FAILURE
codes.meaning: The Windows Installer service couldn't be accessed. Contact your support personnel to verify that the Windows Installer service is properly registered.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_USEREXIT
codes.meaning: The user canceled installation.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_FAILURE
codes.meaning: A fatal error occurred during installation.
codes.use: Read the verbose log (/l*v) and search for the first "Return value 3".

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_SUSPEND
codes.meaning: Installation suspended, incomplete.

codes.name: ERROR_UNKNOWN_PRODUCT
codes.meaning: This action is only valid for products that are currently installed.
codes.use: The product to remove is not installed. Check whether detection matches what is really there.

codes.name: ERROR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE
codes.meaning: The feature identifier isn't registered.

codes.name: ERROR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT
codes.meaning: The component identifier isn't registered.

codes.name: ERROR_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
codes.meaning: This is an unknown property.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE_STATE
codes.meaning: The handle is in an invalid state.

codes.name: ERROR_BAD_CONFIGURATION
codes.meaning: The configuration data for this product is corrupt. Contact your support personnel.

codes.name: ERROR_INDEX_ABSENT
codes.meaning: The component qualifier not present.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_SOURCE_ABSENT
codes.meaning: The installation source for this product isn't available. Verify that the source exists and that you can access it.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_PACKAGE_VERSION
codes.meaning: This installation package can't be installed by the Windows Installer service. You must install a Windows service pack that contains a newer version of the Windows Installer service.

codes.name: ERROR_PRODUCT_UNINSTALLED
codes.meaning: The product is uninstalled.

codes.name: ERROR_BAD_QUERY_SYNTAX
codes.meaning: The SQL query syntax is invalid or unsupported.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_FIELD
codes.meaning: The record field does not exist.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_ALREADY_RUNNING
codes.meaning: Another installation is already in progress. Complete that installation before proceeding with this install. For information about the mutex, see _MSIExecute Mutex.
codes.use: Usually clears by itself. Map it as a retry: Intune's Retry and MECM's Fast Retry run on different schedules.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_PACKAGE_OPEN_FAILED
codes.meaning: This installation package couldn't be opened. Verify that the package exists and is accessible, or contact the application vendor to verify that this is a valid Windows Installer package.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_PACKAGE_INVALID
codes.meaning: This installation package couldn't be opened. Contact the application vendor to verify that this is a valid Windows Installer package.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_UI_FAILURE
codes.meaning: There was an error starting the Windows Installer service user interface. Contact your support personnel.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_LOG_FAILURE
codes.meaning: There was an error opening installation log file. Verify that the specified log file location exists and is writable.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED
codes.meaning: This language of this installation package isn't supported by your system.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_TRANSFORM_FAILURE
codes.meaning: There was an error applying transforms. Verify that the specified transform paths are valid.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_PACKAGE_REJECTED
codes.meaning: This installation is forbidden by system policy. Contact your system administrator.
codes.use: Check the policy that forbids it.

codes.name: ERROR_FUNCTION_NOT_CALLED
codes.meaning: The function couldn't be executed.

codes.name: ERROR_FUNCTION_FAILED
codes.meaning: The function failed during execution.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_TABLE
codes.meaning: An invalid or unknown table was specified.

codes.name: ERROR_DATATYPE_MISMATCH
codes.meaning: The data supplied is the wrong type.

codes.name: ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE
codes.meaning: Data of this type isn't supported.

codes.name: ERROR_CREATE_FAILED
codes.meaning: The Windows Installer service failed to start. Contact your support personnel.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_TEMP_UNWRITABLE
codes.meaning: The Temp folder is either full or inaccessible. Verify that the Temp folder exists and that you can write to it.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED
codes.meaning: This installation package isn't supported on this platform. Contact your application vendor.
codes.use: Check whether a 32-bit or 64-bit package reached the wrong device.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_NOTUSED
codes.meaning: Component isn't used on this machine.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_PACKAGE_OPEN_FAILED
codes.meaning: This patch package couldn't be opened. Verify that the patch package exists and is accessible, or contact the application vendor to verify that this is a valid Windows Installer patch package.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_PACKAGE_INVALID
codes.meaning: This patch package couldn't be opened. Contact the application vendor to verify that this is a valid Windows Installer patch package.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_PACKAGE_UNSUPPORTED
codes.meaning: This patch package can't be processed by the Windows Installer service. You must install a Windows service pack that contains a newer version of the Windows Installer service.

codes.name: ERROR_PRODUCT_VERSION
codes.meaning: Another version of this product is already installed. Installation of this version can't continue. To configure or remove the existing version of this product, use Add/Remove Programs in Control Panel.
codes.use: Check the upgrade path, and whether detection matches what is really installed.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_COMMAND_LINE
codes.meaning: Invalid command line argument. Consult the Windows Installer SDK for detailed command-line help.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_REMOTE_DISALLOWED
codes.meaning: The current user isn't permitted to perform installations from a client session of a server running the Terminal Server role service.

codes.name: ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_INITIATED
codes.meaning: The installer has initiated a restart. This message indicates success.
codes.use: Success, and the installer has started a restart. Map it as a hard reboot.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_TARGET_NOT_FOUND
codes.meaning: The installer can't install the upgrade patch because the program being upgraded may be missing or the upgrade patch updates a different version of the program. Verify that the program to be upgraded exists on your computer and that you have the correct upgrade patch.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_PACKAGE_REJECTED
codes.meaning: The patch package isn't permitted by system policy.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_TRANSFORM_REJECTED
codes.meaning: One or more customizations aren't permitted by system policy.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_REMOTE_PROHIBITED
codes.meaning: Windows Installer doesn't permit installation from a Remote Desktop Connection.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_REMOVAL_UNSUPPORTED
codes.meaning: The patch package isn't a removable patch package.

codes.name: ERROR_UNKNOWN_PATCH
codes.meaning: The patch isn't applied to this product.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_NO_SEQUENCE
codes.meaning: No valid sequence could be found for the set of patches.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_REMOVAL_DISALLOWED
codes.meaning: Patch removal was disallowed by policy.

codes.name: ERROR_INVALID_PATCH_XML
codes.meaning: The XML patch data is invalid.

codes.name: ERROR_PATCH_MANAGED_ADVERTISED_PRODUCT
codes.meaning: Administrative user failed to apply patch for a per-user managed or a per-machine application that'is in advertised state.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_SERVICE_SAFEBOOT
codes.meaning: Windows Installer isn't accessible when the computer is in Safe Mode. Exit Safe Mode and try again or try using system restore to return your computer to a previous state. Available beginning with Windows Installer version 4.0.

codes.name: ERROR_ROLLBACK_DISABLED
codes.meaning: Couldn't perform a multiple-package transaction because rollback has been disabled. Multiple-package installations can't run if rollback is disabled. Available beginning with Windows Installer version 4.5.

codes.name: ERROR_INSTALL_REJECTED
codes.meaning: The app that you're trying to run isn't supported on this version of Windows. A Windows Installer package, patch, or transform that has not been signed by Microsoft can't be installed on an ARM computer.

codes.name: ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_REQUIRED
codes.meaning: A restart is required to complete the install. This message indicates success. This does not include installs where the ForceReboot action is run.
codes.use: Success, with a restart wanted. Map it as a soft reboot in Intune and MECM.

codes.meaning: Application was still detected after uninstall completed
codes.use: Check that the uninstall command really removes what detection looks for.

Application requirement evaluation or detection failed

codes.use: Check that the content is distributed.

codes.meaning: No current or future service window exists to install software updates
codes.use: Check the collection's maintenance windows against the maximum allowed run time.

codes.meaning: Failed to verify the executable file is valid or to construct the associated command line
codes.use: Check the program name and path, and that the program exists on the client.

codes.meaning: Failed to access all the provided program locations. This program may retry if the maximum retry count has not been reached
The content download cannot be performed because there is not enough available space in cache or the disk is full
codes.use: Check the client cache size against the content.

A supported App-V client is not installed
The App-V sftmime command returned failure
An error occurred when querying the App-V WMI provider

codes.use: The code itself says nothing. Read the logs.

One or more arguments are invalid
General access denied error
Unspecified error
Catastrophic failure
Class not registered

codes.use: Content changed after it was distributed. Redistribute it.

codes.meaning: Initialization of the dynamic link library failed. The process is terminating abnormally
WBEM_E_FAILED
WBEM_E_NOT_AVAILABLE
WBEM_E_INVALID_NAMESPACE
The update to be installed is already installed on the system
Operation was not performed because there are no applicable updates
The app failed to install.
codes.use: This error message is displayed when Intune cannot determine the root cause of the Android app installation error. No information was provided by Android during the failure. This error is returned when the APK download succeeded, but the app installation failed. This error may occur more commonly due to a bad APK file that cannot be installed onto the device. A possible cause can be when Google Play Protect blocks the install of the app due to security concerns. Another possible cause of this error is when a device does not support the app. For example, if the app requires API version 21+ and the device currently has API version 19. Intune returns this error for both DA and KNOX devices and although there may be a notification that users can click to retry, if there is an issue with the APK, it will never continue to fail. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed.

codes.meaning: The app installation was canceled because the installation (APK) file was deleted after download, but before installation.
codes.use: The download of the APK succeeded, but before the user installed the app the file was removed from the device. This could happen if there was a large time difference between download and install. For example, the user canceled the original install, waited, and then clicked the notification to try again. This error message is returned this for only DA scenarios. KNOX scenarios can be done silently. We do present a notification to retry so the user can accept instead of cancel. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed.

codes.meaning: The app installation was canceled because the process was restarted during installation.
codes.use: The device was rebooted during the APK installation process, resulting in a canceled installation. This error message is returned for both DA and KNOX devices. Intune presents a notification that users can click to retry. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed.

codes.meaning: The application was not detected after installation completed successfully.
codes.use: The user explicitly uninstalled the app. This error is not returned from the client. It is an error produced when the app was installed at one point, but then the user uninstalled it. This error should only occur for required applications. Users can uninstall non-required apps. This error can only happen in DA. KNOX blocks the uninstall of managed apps. The next sync will repost the notification on the device for the user to install. The user can ignore the notification. This error will continue to be reported until the user installs the app.

codes.meaning: The download failed because of an unknown error.
codes.use: This error occurs when the download fails. This error can commonly occur due to Wi-Fi issues or slow connections. This error is returned for only DA scenarios. For KNOX scenarios, the user is not prompted to install, this can be done silently. Intune presents a notification that users can click to retry. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed.

codes.meaning: The download failed because of an unknown error. The policy will be retried the next time the device syncs.
codes.use: This error occurs when the download fails. This error can commonly occur due to Wi-Fi issues or slow connections. This error is returned for only DA scenarios. For KNOX scenarios, the user is not prompted to install, this can be done silently.

codes.meaning: The end user canceled the app installation.
codes.use: The user explicitly uninstalled the app. This error is returned when the Android OS install activity was canceled by the user. The user pressed the cancel button when the OS install prompt was presented or clicked away from the prompt. This error is returned for only DA scenarios. For KNOX scenarios, the user is not prompted to install, this can be done silently. Intune presents a notification that users can click to retry. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed. Ask the user not to cancel the install.

codes.meaning: The file download process was unexpectedly stopped.
codes.use: The OS stopped the download process before it was complete. This error can occur when the device has low battery or the download is taking too long. This error is returned for only DA scenarios. For KNOX scenarios, the user is not prompted to install, this can be done silently. Intune presents a notification that users can click to retry. If the app is an available app, the notification can be dismissed. However, if the app is required, it cannot be dismissed. Ensure the device has a reliable network connection.

codes.meaning: The file download service was unexpectedly stopped. The policy will be retried the next time the device syncs.
codes.use: The OS ended the download process before it was completed. This error can occur when the device has low battery or the download is taking too long. This error is returned for only DA scenarios. For KNOX scenarios, the user is not prompted to install, this can be done silently. Manually sync the device or wait for 24 hours and check the status.

codes.meaning: The app failed to uninstall.
codes.use: This error is a generic uninstall failure. The OS did not specify why the app failed to uninstall. Some admin apps cannot simply be uninstalled. Check to ensure the app can be uninstalled manually and collect the Company Portal logs if the uninstall fails.

codes.meaning: The app installation APK file used for the upgrade does not match the signature for the current app on the device.
codes.use: Android OS has the limitation of requiring the signing cert for the upgrade version to be exactly the same as the cert used to sign the existing version. If the developer cannot use the same cert to sign the new version, you will need to uninstall the existing app and re-deploy the new app rather than upgrade the existing app.

codes.meaning: The end user canceled the app installation.
codes.use: Educate the user to accept the Intune deployed app and install the app when prompted.

codes.meaning: Uninstall of the app was canceled because the process was restarted during installation.
codes.use: The app install process was terminated by the OS or the device was restarted. Retry the install and collect Company Portal logs if this error occurs again.

codes.meaning: The app installation APK file cannot be installed because it was not signed.
codes.use: By default, Android OS requires apps to be signed. Ensure the app is signed before deployment.

codes.meaning: Apple MDM Agent error: App installation command failed with no error reason specified. Retry app installation.
codes.use: Apple MDM Agent returned that the installation command failed.

codes.meaning: Network connection on the client was lost or interrupted. Later attempts should succeed in a better network environment.
codes.use: The network connection was lost while the updated download service URL was sent to the device. Specifically, a server with the specified hostname could not be found.

codes.meaning: Could not retrieve license for the app with iTunes Store ID
codes.use: Sync the associated VPP token, then sync the device with Intune. If the issue persists, remove group assignment and reassign the VPP app as device-licensed. If the issue still persists, revoke the app license from the device by navigating to Apps > iOS > select VPP app > App licenses > select device. Then, revoke license and try re-assigning the app to the user group or device group. If the issue still persists, revoke all VPP licenses for the device by going to Devices > iOS > select device > Overview > Revoke licenses, then retire the device and re-enroll to Intune.

codes.meaning: iOS/iPadOS device is currently busy.
codes.use: The iOS/iPadOS device was busy, which resulted in an error. The device was locked. The user needs to unlock the device to install the app.

codes.meaning: The app installation has failed. (ErrorUserEnrollmentUnsupported)
codes.use: The VPP app is deployed with the Device licensing type but only the User licensing type is supported for BYOD (bring your own device) devices enrolled with account driven Apple User Enrollment. Change the licensing type for the assignments or create a separate assignment for the users.

codes.meaning: The app installation has failed.
codes.use: An app installation failure occurred. iOS/iPadOS Console logs are needed to troubleshoot this error.

codes.meaning: The app is managed, but has expired or been removed by the user.
codes.use: Either the user explicitly uninstalled the app, or the app is expired but failed to download, or the app detection does not match the response from the device. Additionally, this error could occur based on an iOS/iPadOS 9.2.2 platform bug.

codes.meaning: The app is scheduled for installation, but needs a redemption code to complete the transaction.
codes.use: This error typically occurs with iOS Store apps which are paid apps.

codes.meaning: Unknown error.
codes.use: An unknown app installation error occurred. This error code can be returned for multiple reasons, one of which is an expired VPP token in Intune. As a general recommendation, whenever an unknown error is encountered, ensure that the Volume Purchase Program (VPP) token is checked to verify that it's current and functional.

codes.meaning: The application was not detected after installation completed successfully.
codes.use: The app detection process did not match with the response from the device.

codes.meaning: The user rejected the offer to install the app.
codes.use: During initial app install, the user clicked cancel. Ask the user to accept the install request the next time.

codes.meaning: The user rejected the offer to update the app.
codes.use: The end user clicked cancel during the update process. Deploy as required or educate the user to accept the upgrade prompt.

codes.meaning: Unknown error
codes.use: An unknown app installation error occurred. This is the resulting error when other errors have not occurred.

codes.meaning: Can only install VPP apps on Shared iPad.
codes.use: The apps must be obtained using Apple Volume Purchase Program to install on a Shared iPad.

codes.meaning: Can't install apps when App Store is disabled.
codes.use: The App Store must be enabled for the user to install the app.

codes.meaning: Can't find VPP license for app.
codes.use: Try revoking and reassigning the app license.

codes.meaning: Can't install system apps with your MDM provider.
codes.use: Installing apps that are pre-installed by the iOS/iPadOS operating system is not a supported scenario.

codes.meaning: Can't install apps when device is in Lost Mode.
codes.use: All use of the device is blocked in Lost Mode. Disable Lost Mode to install apps.

codes.meaning: Can't install apps when device is in kiosk mode.
codes.use: Try adding this device to an exclude group for kiosk mode configuration policy to install apps.

codes.meaning: Can't install 32-bit apps on this device.
codes.use: The device doesn't support installing 32-bit apps. Try deploying the 64-bit version of the app.

codes.meaning: User must sign in to the App Store.
codes.use: The user needs to sign in to the App Store before the app can be installed.

codes.meaning: Unknown problem. Please try again.
codes.use: The app installation failed due to an unknown reason. Try again later.

codes.meaning: The app installation failed. Intune will try again the next time the device syncs.
codes.use: The app installation encountered a device error. Sync the device to try installing the app again.

codes.meaning: License Assignment failed with Apple error 'No VPP licenses remaining'
codes.use: This behavior is by design. To resolve this, purchase additional VPP licenses or reclaim licenses from users no longer targeted.

codes.meaning: App Install Failure 12024: Unknown cause.
codes.use: Apple hasn't given us sufficient information to determine why the install failed. Nothing to report.

codes.meaning: Needed app configuration policy not present, ensure policy is targeted to same groups.
codes.use: App requires app config but no app config is targeted. Admin should make sure the groups the app is targeted to also has the required app config targeted to the groups.

codes.meaning: Device VPP licensing is only applicable for iOS/iPadOS 9.0+ devices.
codes.use: Upgrade affected iOS/iPadOS devices to iOS/iPadOS 9.0+.

codes.meaning: The application is installed on the device but is unmanaged.
codes.use: This error only happens to LOB apps. The app was installed outside of Intune. To address this error, uninstall the app from the device. The next time the device sync happens, the device should install the app from Intune.

codes.meaning: User declined app management
codes.use: Ask the user to accept app management.

codes.meaning: Unknown error.
codes.use: This error happens to iOS store apps, but the error scenario is unknown.

codes.meaning: The latest version of the app failed to update from an earlier version.
codes.use: This error message is displayed if the app is installed and managed but with the incorrect version on the device. This situation includes when a device has received a command to update an app but the new version has not yet been installed and reported back. This error will be reported for the first check-in of a device after the upgrade has been deployed, and will occur until the device reports that the new version is installed, or fails due to a different error.

codes.meaning: Your connection to Intune timed out.
codes.use: App Manifest validation failure due to network connectivity(timeout)

codes.meaning: You lost connection to the Internet.
codes.use: App Manifest validation failure due to network connectivity(Cannot Find Host)

codes.meaning: You lost connection to the Internet.
codes.use: App Manifest validation failure due to network connectivity(Connection Lost)

codes.meaning: You lost connection to the Internet.
codes.use: App Manifest validation failure due to network connectivity(Not Connected to internet)

codes.meaning: The secure connection failed.
codes.use: App Manifest validation failure due to network connectivity(Secure Connection Failed)

codes.meaning: CannotConnectToITunesStoreError
codes.use: App install failed due to failure to Connect To ITunes Store

codes.meaning: The VPP App has an update available
codes.use: This code is returned when a VPP app is installed but there is a newer version available.

codes.meaning: Can't enforce app uninstall setting. Retry installing the app.
codes.use: The app is already installed on the device but the "uninstall on retire" setting does not match the configured value. Advise the user to request the app-install from Company Portal to attempt applying the "uninstall on retire" setting again.

codes.meaning: To install this app, you must have a sideloading-enabled system. Make sure that the app package is signed with a trusted signature and installed on a domain-joined device that has the AllowAllTrustedApps policy enabled, or a device that has a Windows Sideloading license with the AllowAllTrustedApps policy enabled. For more information, see Troubleshooting packaging, deployment, and query of Windows Store apps.

To install this app, you must have a sideloading-enabled system. Make sure that the app package is signed with a trusted signature and installed on a domain-joined device that has the AllowAllTrustedApps policy enabled, or a device that has a Windows Sideloading license with the AllowAllTrustedApps policy enabled. For more information, see Troubleshooting packaging, deployment, and query of Windows Store apps.
The package could not be opened.
codes.use: The package is unsigned. The publisher name does not match the signing certificate subject. Check the AppxPackagingOM event log for information. For more information, see Troubleshooting packaging, deployment, and query of Windows Store apps.

codes.meaning: The package failed update, dependency, or conflict validation.
codes.use: The incoming package conflicts with an installed package. A specified package dependency is not found. The package does not support the correct processor architecture. Check the AppXDeployment-Server event log for information. For more information, see Troubleshooting packaging, deployment, and query of Windows Store apps.

codes.meaning: The provided package is already installed, and reinstallation of the package is blocked. You could receive this error if you are installing a package that is not identical to the package that is already installed. Confirm the digital signature is also part of the package. When a package is rebuilt or re-signed, that package is no longer bitwise identical to the previously installed package.
codes.use: Increment the version number of the app, then rebuild and re-sign the package. Remove the old package for every user on the system before you install the new package. For more information, see Troubleshooting packaging, deployment, and query of Windows Store apps.

codes.meaning: Application installation succeeded but application is not detected. The app was deployed successfully by Intune, then subsequently uninstalled.
codes.use: Check the detection rule, as for MECM 0x87D00324; a self-updating app can also stop matching the version it was detected by.

codes.meaning: An unexpected error occurred during installation. Check the installation logs for additional information.
